sub: Named after “al-qadr”, the Night of Decree, in ayah 1
theme: The Quran was sent down on one blessed night, better than a thousand months. Angels fill the earth with Allah’s decrees, and it is peace until dawn.
story: Reports differ on whether it came in Makkah or Madinah. Placed right after Al-ʿAlaq, it tells when the Quran’s revelation began: on the Night of Decree, in Ramadan.

Reportedly the Prophet ﷺ told of a man from the Children of Israel who fought in Allah’s cause for a thousand months, and the Muslims were amazed. Another report says he felt his ummah’s lives were short.
So Allah gave this ummah one night worth more than a thousand months, returning every year until the end of time.

sections.title: The Quran came down on Laylat al-Qadr, better than a thousand months
sections.meaning: Allah sent the Quran down on Laylat al-Qadr. What will tell you what that night is? It is better than a thousand months: good deeds in it outweigh a thousand months without it.
points: We sent it down on the Night of Decree
What will make you know what it is?
sections.matters: It shows the Quran’s worth: the night it came down became the greatest night of the year. And it hands every believer a night that can outweigh a whole lifetime.
sections.story: Reportedly the Prophet ﷺ told of a man of the Children of Israel who fought for Allah a thousand months, and the Muslims marvelled. Ayah 3 was revealed: this night is better than all those months.
explained: Innā anzalnāhu: We sent it down. The Quran came down whole to the lowest heaven on this night, then in parts to the Prophet ﷺ over twenty-three years. Or: its revelation began on this night. Al-qadr means honour, and also decree: the year’s matters are set out in it.

Wa mā adrāka: its worth is beyond what you can guess. Good deeds in it are better than a thousand months, over eighty-three years, without it. Whoever stands in prayer on it with faith, hoping for reward, has his past sins forgiven.
teaches: Honour the Quran: it made a night great.
One night of worship can outweigh a lifetime.
Stand in prayer that night with faith and hope.
Whoever misses its good has truly missed out.
sections.hook: Laylat al-qadr comes three times in three ayat: ending 1, ending 2, opening 3. The surah never names the Quran; it just says “it” (anzalnāhu).

sections.title: That night angels and Jibrīl descend with decrees; peace until dawn
sections.meaning: On that night the angels and the Rūḥ, Jibrīl, come down in crowds by their Lord’s permission with every matter decreed. It is peace, all of it, until the break of dawn.
points: Angels and Jibrīl descend with every decree
Peace until the rising of dawn
sections.matters: It shows why the night is so great: the angels fill the earth. And it ends with peace, so the believer spends the whole night, from sunset to dawn, in calm worship.
sections.story: No specific incident. The night falls in Ramadan, most likely on an odd night of the last ten, and it returns every year.
explained: Tanazzalu: the angels descend in great numbers, more than the pebbles on earth, and with them ar-Rūḥ, Jibrīl, named separately from the rest. They come bi-idhni rabbihim, by permission, min kulli amr: with every matter Allah has decreed for the coming year.

Salāmun hiya: it is all peace and good, with no evil in it; Shayṭān can do no harm, and the angels greet the believers. It lasts ḥattā maṭlaʿ al-fajr, until dawn. The Prophet ﷺ taught ʿĀʾishah to say: “O Allah, You are Pardoning and love to pardon, so pardon me.”
teaches: Seek the night in the odd nights of Ramadan’s last ten.
Ask Allah often for pardon that night.
The angels come down; be found worshipping.
Its blessing lasts all night, until dawn.
sections.hook: Ayah 4 is the longest in the surah. The surah opens with laylah, night (1), and closes with al-fajr, dawn (5).

groups.text: Allah sent the Quran down on the Night of Decree.
What will tell you what it is? It is better than a thousand months.
Angels and Jibrīl descend with every decree, and it is peace until dawn.

1.explain: Innā anzalnāhu: We sent “it”, the Quran, down on laylat al-qadr, whole to the lowest heaven, then gradually. Or its revelation began that night. Qadr means honour, and also decree.

2.explain: Wa mā adrāka: a question that shows how great the night is, beyond what you could know on your own.

3.explain: Good deeds on this one night are better than those of a thousand months without it, more than eighty-three years. The number may simply mean a very large amount.
3.why: Reportedly the Prophet ﷺ spoke of a man from the Children of Israel who fought in Allah’s cause for a thousand months, and the Muslims marvelled. Another report: he felt his ummah’s lives were short, and this night was given to them.

4.explain: Tanazzalu: the angels come down in crowds, with ar-Rūḥ, Jibrīl, by their Lord’s permission, min kulli amr: with every matter decreed for the year ahead, such as lifespans and provision.

5.explain: Salāmun hiya: it is peace, safe from every evil; Shayṭān can do no harm in it, and angels greet the believers. It lasts from sunset ḥattā maṭlaʿ al-fajr, until dawn.
